t: The 'tabular premium' of a plan refers to
o: the premium after deducting all rebates
the premium per ₹1,000 sum assured shown in the rate table for a given age and term, before rebates or extras
the premium inclusive of rider charges
e: Tabular premium is the base rate from the insurer's premium table; rebates, loadings and extras are applied to it.

t: The first private sector life insurers after liberalisation were granted certificates of registration by IRDA in the year
e: After the IRDA Act 1999, the regulator was constituted in April 2000 and the first private life insurers were registered in 2000.

t: Most critical illness riders require the insured to survive a specified number of days after diagnosis before the benefit is payable. This is called the
e: The survival period (often 30 days) distinguishes a CI claim from a death claim; the waiting period is the initial period after issue during which no CI claim is admitted.

t: The National Pension System is regulated by
e: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority regulates NPS, although annuities at exit are bought from IRDAI-regulated life insurers.

t: The mortality table currently prescribed for valuation and commonly used for pricing by Indian life insurers is
e: IALM 2012-14 is the latest Indian assured lives table published by the Institute of Actuaries of India and prescribed by IRDAI.

t: Under a double endowment assurance, the benefit on survival to maturity is
o: the basic sum assured, while death benefit is twice
twice the sum assured, while death benefit is the basic sum assured
the basic sum assured with double bonus
e: Double endowment pays 2 × SA on maturity and 1 × SA on earlier death, making it a saving-oriented plan.

t: A ULIP fund is worth ₹2,40,000 and the policyholder holds 12,000 units. If ₹60,000 is withdrawn at the current NAV, the number of units cancelled is
The guaranteed surrender value is computed on the premiums paid
o: including extra premiums but excluding GST
excluding extra premiums, rider premiums and taxes
e: GSV = GSV factor × total base premiums paid (net of extras, riders and taxes) plus surrender value of accrued bonus.

t: For an 'ordinary revival', the insurer normally requires
o: payment of all arrears of premium with interest and satisfactory evidence of continued good health
a fresh proposal form and medical at the insurer's cost
e: Revival is at the insurer's discretion; evidence of health may be a declaration of good health or a medical report depending on amount and duration.

t: Under a group credit life (loan protection) scheme sold through a bank, the master policyholder is
o: the lending bank or financial institution
e: The lender holds the master policy and members are the borrowers; the cover usually reduces in line with the outstanding loan.

t: A life assured has been missing for several years. Under the rules of evidence, death may be presumed if he has not been heard of for
e: Section 108 of the Indian Evidence Act (now Section 111 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023) presumes death after seven years of being unheard of.

t: 'Twisting' in life insurance refers to an agent
o: selling to a person without insurable interest
inducing a policyholder to lapse or surrender an existing policy to buy a new one, to the policyholder's detriment
e: Twisting is a prohibited practice because the policyholder loses accumulated benefits and pays fresh acquisition costs.

t: If the life assured under a ULIP commits suicide within 12 months of commencement, the nominee is entitled to
o: the fund value as on the date of intimation of death
e: For linked policies the suicide clause provides the fund value on intimation; for non-linked policies it is at least 80% of premiums paid or surrender value.

t: Which of the following is treated as non-standard age proof by Indian life insurers?
o: PAN card with date of birth
e: Horoscopes, self-declarations and elder's declarations are non-standard and attract extra premium or restrictions.

t: A top-up premium paid under a ULIP is
o: added to the fund with no additional sum assured
used to pay future regular premiums
treated like a single premium with its own lock-in and an associated minimum sum assured
e: Top-ups buy additional units and must carry a minimum sum assured (1.25 times for a single premium) with their own five-year lock-in.

t: For a one-year term assurance of ₹5,00,000 at a mortality rate of 4 per 1,000, the net single premium ignoring interest and expenses is
A policy was absolutely assigned to a bank as security. On death of the life assured while the assignment subsists, the claim is payable to
e: Absolute assignment transfers all rights, including the right to receive the claim, to the assignee.

t: A group superannuation scheme is designed to provide
o: lump sum on accidental death of employees
e: Superannuation funds accumulate employer (and employee) contributions to provide retirement pension.

t: Premium paid for a pension/annuity plan of a life insurer qualifies for deduction under
o: Section 80CCC, within the overall limit of ₹1.5 lakh under Section 80CCE
e: 80CCC covers contributions to insurers' pension plans and shares the ₹1.5 lakh ceiling with 80C and 80CCD(1).

t: The tabular premium is ₹40 per ₹1,000 sum assured and a high sum assured rebate of ₹2 per ₹1,000 applies. The annual premium for ₹10,00,000 before any mode rebate is
The GST rate applicable to the renewal premium of a traditional endowment policy (before the September 2025 exemption) was
e: Endowment premiums attracted GST at 4.5% in the first year and 2.25% on renewals; term premiums attracted 18%.

t: For an early death claim, in addition to the basic documents, the insurer usually calls for
o: the proposer's income tax return for the current year
a fresh medical report of the nominee
hospital treatment records and the employer's leave/attendance certificate
e: Early claims are investigated to rule out non-disclosure, so past treatment and leave records are examined.

t: A life assured paid monthly premiums for 9 months and then stopped. He dies three months after the grace period expired. Under the 2024 product regulations
o: the full sum assured is payable
a paid-up sum assured for 9/12 of the first year is payable
nothing is payable, as the policy lapsed before acquiring any paid-up or surrender value
e: A policy acquires surrender/paid-up value only after the first full year's premium is paid; before that, lapse results in forfeiture.

t: The effect of an absolute assignment of a policy on an existing nomination is that
o: the nomination is automatically cancelled, except where the assignment is to the insurer for a loan
e: Section 39 provides that assignment cancels nomination, but an assignment to the insurer against a loan merely suspends the nominee's right.

t: The surrender value available under a pure term assurance policy (regular premium) is
e: Term plans build no reserve, so no surrender value arises except under return-of-premium variants.

t: An agent's role at the time of a death claim is to
o: decide whether the claim is payable
receive the claim cheque on behalf of the nominee
charge a fee for claim assistance
assist the nominee in completing the claim forms and arranging the required documents
e: Post-sale service, including claim assistance, is part of the agent's duty under the code of conduct.

t: A 35-year-old proposer earns ₹8 lakh per annum. If the insurer's financial underwriting allows 20 times annual income for this age band, the maximum total sum assured permissible is
e: ₹8,00,000 × 20 = ₹1,60,00,000; existing cover with all insurers is counted against this limit.

t: A policy has run for six years and the life assured dies of natural causes. The insurer should
o: repudiate if any pre-existing illness is found
refer the matter to the Ombudsman
settle the claim on receipt of basic documents within 15 days, as it is a non-early claim and Section 45 bars questioning
e: After three years a policy cannot be questioned on any ground, so non-early natural death claims are settled on basic documents.

t: A policy is conditionally assigned to the policyholder's wife with the condition that it reverts if she predeceases him. The wife dies first. The policy
o: passes to the wife's legal heirs
e: Conditional assignments contain a reversion clause; absolute assignments pass all rights permanently.

t: A 'convertible whole life' policy allows the policyholder to
o: convert the policy into an annuity at any time
convert the sum assured into units
convert the whole life policy into an endowment after a specified period without fresh medical evidence
convert the policy to a term plan at reduced premium
e: It starts as a low-premium whole life plan and may be converted to an endowment, typically after five years, when the policyholder can afford higher premium.

t: An annuity 'certain for 15 years and life thereafter' means
o: payments are made only if the annuitant survives 15 years
the purchase price is returned after 15 years
payments are guaranteed for 15 years even if the annuitant dies, and continue for life if he survives
e: The guaranteed period protects the nominee against early death; after it, payments continue only during the annuitant's lifetime.

t: If the original policy bond is found after a duplicate policy has been issued, the policyholder should
o: sell the original to the assignee
return the original to the insurer, since only one policy document can be in force
e: The indemnity bond executed for the duplicate obliges the policyholder to surrender the original if traced.

t: Mr A wishes to insure the life of his adult brother who lives separately and earns independently. The insurer will
o: accept, as blood relations always have insurable interest
generally decline, as insurable interest is not presumed between adult siblings
accept provided the brother is below age 40
accept only on a term plan
e: Insurable interest between siblings is not presumed; it must be demonstrated through actual financial dependence.

t: Keyman insurance in India is permitted to be written only under
e: IRDAI guidelines (consistent with CBDT's view) restrict keyman insurance to term plans so that it remains a protection, not a savings, product.

t: For private life insurers in India, the channel that contributes the largest share of individual new business premium is
e: Private insurers depend heavily on bank partners; for LIC the dominant channel remains individual agents.

t: An insurer reports a 61st-month persistency of 50%. The correct interpretation is that
o: half of the policies will mature in the 61st month
only half of the policies sold five years ago are still being renewed
half of the maturity claims were paid within 61 days
the insurer retains 50% of its agents for five years
e: The 61st-month persistency tracks policies that have completed five years; 50% implies half of them have lapsed or been surrendered.

t: Under IRDAI micro-insurance regulations, entities such as NGOs, self-help groups and micro-finance institutions may distribute micro-insurance products by being appointed as
e: Micro-insurance agents are a special intermediary category created to reach low-income segments.

t: A policy issued in 2015 has a sum assured of ₹5 lakh and annual premium of ₹60,000. The maturity proceeds are
o: exempt because total premium is below ₹5 lakh
fully taxable, as premium exceeds 10% of the sum assured
taxable only on the bonus portion
e: For policies issued on or after 1 April 2012, exemption requires premium ≤ 10% of SA; ₹60,000 is 12%.

t: The Net Asset Value (NAV) of a ULIP fund is computed as
o: total premium received ÷ number of policies
fund management charge ÷ number of units
(market value of investments + current assets − current liabilities and provisions) ÷ number of units outstanding
e: NAV reflects the per-unit value of the fund after accounting for assets, liabilities and charges.

t: Under the 'special revival' scheme, a lapsed policy is revived by
o: using the surrender value to pay arrears
shifting the date of commencement so that only one year's premium is paid, with premium recalculated at the new age
e: Special revival re-dates the policy; it is generally allowed once, only if the lapsed policy has not acquired surrender value and the lapse is within a limited period.

t: A creditor has lent ₹10 lakh to a debtor. The creditor's insurable interest in the debtor's life is
o: limited to ten times the loan
limited to the amount of the loan plus interest
nil, since only relatives have insurable interest
e: Creditor-debtor insurable interest is restricted to the financial loss the creditor would suffer, i.e. the debt and interest.

t: 'Adverse selection' (anti-selection) in life insurance refers to
o: the insurer selecting only wealthy clients
the tendency of persons with higher-than-average risk to seek insurance more actively
the agent choosing the wrong plan for the customer
e: Underwriting exists primarily to counter anti-selection and keep the pool's mortality close to the pricing assumption.

t: Under a joint life endowment on a 'first death' basis, on the death of one of the two lives
o: half the sum assured is paid and the policy continues
nothing is paid until the second death
the sum assured is paid and the policy terminates
premiums are waived and the policy continues to maturity
e: First-death joint life policies pay once, on the earlier of first death or maturity, and then cease.

t: The minimum guaranteed interest rate on the Discontinued Policy Fund of a ULIP is currently
e: IRDAI prescribes a minimum guaranteed return on the discontinued policy fund, currently 4% p.a.

t: A 'cash bonus' differs from a reversionary bonus in that it is
o: paid to the policyholder in cash each year when declared, rather than attached to the policy
e: Cash bonus gives immediate benefit; reversionary bonus is payable with the sum assured on claim.

t: Another name for the money-back policy is
e: Money-back plans are technically anticipated endowments because part of the sum assured is paid in anticipation of maturity.

t: Under a 'return of premium' term assurance plan, on survival to the end of the term the policyholder receives
o: the total premiums paid, excluding GST and rider premiums
nothing, as it is a pure term plan
e: TROP plans refund base premiums on survival; taxes and rider premiums are not refunded.

t: A life rated at '+100% extra mortality' is expected to experience mortality that is
e: Extra mortality is expressed as a percentage of standard; +100% means standard plus 100%, i.e. double.

t: A participating endowment of ₹3,00,000 has earned simple reversionary bonus at ₹45 per ₹1,000 sum assured for 6 years. The vested bonus is
If an insurer increases the expense loading in its premium basis, the effect will be that
o: the office premium rises while the pure (net) premium is unchanged
both pure and office premium fall
the pure premium rises while office premium is unchanged
neither pure nor office premium changes
e: Pure premium depends only on mortality and interest; expense loading affects only the office (gross) premium.
